minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 26, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:00 p.m., on September 26, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 21, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths (arrived at 6:40 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Mary Binning, Assistant City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation (Paragraph (1) of Subdivision
  (d) of Section 54956.9) Webster v. City of Mission Viejo (CWC1915666) Court file 30-
  2017-00912657 - CU-EI-CXC.

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators; Housing Authority of Mission Viejo;
  Property: APN 740-112-03; Negotiating Parties: Jamboree Housing; Agency
  Negotiators: Executive Director Wilberg and Community Development Director
  Lister; Under Negotiation: Price, Terms of Payment.

City Council Minutes  1  September 26, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

Assistant City Attorney Mary Binning noted that the City Council discussed two Closed Session
matters. They provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation on the Hearts for Hearts Foundation

  The City Council received the presentation from Mai Griffith, founder of the Hearts for
  Hearts Foundation.

P2.  Hurricane Help Campaign for Middle School in Port Aransas, Texas

  The Council received the presentation from Community Services Commission and
  Mission Viejo Activities Committee Member, Cathy Allen. Director of Recreation and
  Community Services Mark Nix appeared in a video message discussing the campaign to
  help Port Aransas, Texas.

P3.  Drug Prevention Coalition Update and Monitor, Secure, and Destroy Campaign

  The City Council received the presentation from Community Services Supervisor, Leslie
  Rea-McDonald.

P4.  Presentation by Santa Margarita Water District on the National Award for the
  Lake Advanced Purified Water Project

  The Council received the presentation from Santa Margarita Water District's Deputy
  General Manager, Don Bunts.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

*Council Member Raths arrived at 6:40 p.m.

Michael Rotcher, M.V.: discussed a new program called Community Choice Energy (CCE) which,
he said, is a market-based program bringing local control, freedom of choice and competition into

City Council Minutes  2  September 26, 2017
 the electricity marketplace. Mr. Rotcher stated that the program would be a win-win for residents,
cities and economics and he offered to share more information with staff and the Council Members.

Deborah Cunningham-Skurnik, M.V.: said that the Council’s adoption of an ordinance making it
illegal to sleep in parks overnight criminalizes and humiliates the homeless. She noted that she
was recently elected as Region 18 Director for the California Democratic Party and one of her
duties is to recruit and vet candidates running for office. She said there will be quite an awakening
for those up for re-election next year.

Hoiyin Ip, representing the Sierra Club (no address/city listed): thanked the Council for keeping
Mission Viejo a charming place. She discussed the State’s ban of trash in waterways and she asked
what the City can do to help eliminate single-use trash bags such as a “bring your own” (bag)
campaign.

Ryan Reza Farsai, M.V.: stated that the City is illegally operating an electronic sign on his ARCO
station property at La Paz and Marguerite and presented documents to try and prove his position.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of September 12, 2017, as
  presented.

3.  Check Register Dated September 1, 2017 in the Amount of $919,204.57

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated September 8, 2017 in the Amount of $334,317.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.
City Council Minutes  3  September 26, 2017
 5.  Claim Against the City - Susana Coral, Heir of Shireen Tabatabai

  Rejected claim.

6.  Claim Against the City - Su, a Minor

  Rejected claim.

7.  Claim Against the City - Alejo, a Minor

  Rejected claim.

8.  Review and Approval of Amended Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the
  17-18B Fiscal Period of January 1, 2018 to June 30, 2018

  Adopted Successor Agency Resolution 17-02 Approving the Amendment of the
  Recognized Obligation Payment Schedule for the 17-18B fiscal period of January 1, 2018,
  to June 30, 2018, subject to submittal to and review by the Oversight Board and by the
  Department of Finance under the Dissolution Law, California Health and Safety Code,
  Division 24, Part 1.85, and Authorizing Posting and Transmittal Thereof.

9.  El Toro Road Traffic Signal Synchronization (Project P) Cooperative Agreement

  Approved Cooperative Agreement No. C-7-1827 with the Orange County Transportation
  Authority for El Toro Road Traffic Signal Synchronization (CIP 17231).

10.  Orange County Transportation Authority 2017-2018 Comprehensive Transportation
  Funding Program Call-for-Projects

  Adopted Resolution 17-41 Approving the Submittal of the Los Alisos Boulevard Corridor
  Improvement Project to the OCTA for Funding Under the Competitive Measure M2
  Regional Transportation Signal Synchronization Program (Project P).

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

11.  Service Cost Recovery Study

  At the hour of 6:55 p.m., Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing and noted that this
  matter will be continued to a future meeting. She asked if there were any interested parties
  present to make comments this evening and hearing no requests to speak, Mayor Bucknum
  closed the Public Hearing at 6:57 p.m.

City Council Minutes  4  September 26, 2017
 12.  An Extension, for a Maximum Period of One Year to Urgency Ordinance 16-321, an
  Interim Zoning Ordinance Adopted as an Urgency Measure Pursuant to Government
  Code Section 65858, and Establishing a Temporary Moratorium on the Approval of
  Permits for New or Expanded Uses Involving, Directly or Indirectly, the Collective
  Transport of Groups of People and Associated Group Assembly in the City

  Mayor Bucknum opened the Public Hearing at 6:58 p.m.

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented the staff report.

  Hearing no requests to speak, Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing at 7:00 p.m.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve an extension, for a maximum period of one year, to Urgency Ordinance 16-321,
  an Interim Zoning Ordinance adopted as an urgency measure pursuant to Government
  Code Section 65858, and establishing a temporary moratorium on the approval of permits
  for new or expanded uses involving, directly or indirectly, the collective transport of groups
  of people and associated group assembly in the City; and (2) direct staff to further study
  and explore appropriate regulatory options and return with a recommendation to City
  Council regarding the structuring of zoning over a new use/ facility and the expansion of
  an existing use/ facility involving directly or indirectly, the collective transport of groups
  of people and associated group assembly.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

13.  SB 1: Road Repair and Accountability Act Project List

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-42 Amending the Fiscal Year 2017-18 Budget to Incorporate Additional
  Required Information to the List of Projects Funded by SB 1: The Road Repair and
  Accountability Act, and Transfer Budgeted Revenue and Expenditures to a New Fund.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  September 26, 2017
 NEW BUSINESS

14.  Authorizing an Amendment to the Contract for California Public Employees’
  Retirement System to Implement Government Code section 20516(a)

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt
  Resolution 17-43 Declaring Its Intention to Approve an Amendment to Contract Between
  the Board of Administration, California Public Employees' Retirement System and the City
  Council of the City of Mission Viejo; and (2) introduce Ordinance 17-325 Authorizing an
  Amendment to the Contract Between the City Council of the City of Mission Viejo and the
  Board of Administration of the California Public Employees' Retirement System.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

15.  2017 Citywide Speed Limit Update

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to introduce
  Ordinance 17-326 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

16.  Memorandum of Understanding for Cost and Efficiency Study of Orange County
  Sheriff’s Department Contract Law Enforcement Services

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to (1) approve the
  Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Mission Viejo and the Orange County
  Sheriff's Department Contract Cities for the Orange County Sheriff-Coroner Department's
  Contract Law Enforcement Cost and Efficient Study and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the Agreement; (2) approve issuance of Request for Proposals; and (3) adopt
  Resolution 17-44 Amending FY 2017/18 Budget.

City Council Minutes  6  September 26, 2017
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS

17.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief Steve Edwards presented an update on the Corona fire noting that
  approximately 2,000 acres have burned. He said the fire has only been contained to 5%
  however the fire activity was reduced greatly today.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell mentioned the public comment by Michael Rotcher earlier in the
meeting and said he has met with Mr. Rotcher to discuss Community Choice Energy. He is going
to do a little more research, then invite Mr. Rotcher to make a presentation to the Economic
Development Committee before presenting to the City Council. Council Member Goodell said
that it is an interesting idea to allow residents freedom of choice with electricity and it would
provide more competition and ability to buy energy from green providers.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley discussed her attendance at Supervisor Lisa Bartlett’s South County
Veterans Resource Fair at Saddleback College and several Drug Prevention Coalition meetings.
She said there is a lot of work to be done but it is very good that Mission Viejo has recognized the
need for drug addiction awareness and action. She noted that when she went to the first Coalition
meeting a number of parents in attendance had lost children to drug addiction and every one of
them said that their child began with marijuana. She expressed that this furthers her concern that
marijuana is now legal for adults in California. Council Member Kelley committed to continue
attending meetings and said that it is good for the Council to know what is going on with the Drug
Coalition Committee and to distribute information to the community. She announced that she was
sorry to miss the Mission Viejo Country Club’s 50th anniversary celebration but she was proud to
attend her son-in-law’s induction into the Athletic Hall of fame at Cal Poly University that day. In
conclusion, Council Member Kelley congratulated the City’s Building Manager, Jay Elbettar, who
received the honor of being appointed President of the International Code Council.
City Council Minutes  7  September 26, 2017
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths noted that he was late to the meeting because attended the Irvine City
Council meeting to testify on behalf of veterans for a new veteran cemetery at the Irvine Great
Park. He spoke before the City Council and offered that they were only asking for 125 acres of
land on the 6,000-acre Great Park parcel and he said it sounded like it will be approved. Council
Member Raths discussed his attendance at the Veterans Resource Fair where he was honored to
represent the City. He also discussed his knowledge of the Brown Act and how it can sometimes
be difficult to be fully informed due to certain regulations. He apologized for his frustration at the
last meeting on the civic core area plan and he said he has since been updated and he feels better
about what has been done. His remaining concern is about moving forward without concrete ideas
from the business owners. Finally, Council Member Raths shared that some other cities are getting
away from their $60,000 contracts with Townsend Public Affairs and instead doing a pay as you
go program for legislative services.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs mentioned that he will be attending the Mobility 21 convention where the
Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) will receive the National Innovations Partnership award
for settling a 13-year lawsuit and moving forward on transportation mobility in South County. He
said he looks forward to accepting the award that with TCA CEO Mike Kraman along with the
Save the San Onofre Coalition. At the convention, he will also participate on a panel to discuss
how technology is outpacing funding and how transportation agencies are working to create greater
quality of life and mobility in the region.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum announce that she attended the celebration for the 50th anniversary of the Mission
Viejo Country Club where they unveiled a special clock. She asked that at the next City Council
Meeting, staff present a progress report, with pictures, on the Marguerite Aquatics Complex
renovation.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:08 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Steve Bollweg, to Tuesday, October 10,
2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of October 10, 2017

City Council Minutes  8  September 26, 2017
